guarantees.claim: rx_valid is always equal to rx_valid_q.
rx_data gets sreg_q[8:1] when parity_enable is true; otherwise rx_data gets sreg_q[9:2].
frame_err is set to rx_valid_q & ~sreg_q[10], flagging a frame error when rx_valid_q is high and the stop bit (sreg_q[10]) is low.
rx_parity_err is set to parity_enable & rx_valid_q & (^{sreg_q[9:1],parity_odd}), detecting a parity error when parity is enabled, valid is high, and the computed parity does not match.

assumptions.claim: When rx_valid_q is set, sreg_q must hold a complete UART frame with start bit at bit 0, data bits mapped according to parity_enable (bits 1-8 if enabled, otherwise bits 2-9), parity bit (if enabled) at bit 9, and stop bit at bit 10.
assumptions.risk: If upstream shift logic places bits in wrong positions, rx_data, frame_err, and rx_parity_err will be incorrect.

assumptions.claim: parity_enable and parity_odd must be stable and must correctly reflect the UART configuration for the duration of the frame and the valid window.
assumptions.risk: Toggling or mismatched values will cause wrong data mapping or parity detection.

uncertain_points.claim: rx_data is output directly from sreg_q even when frame_err or rx_parity_err is asserted, exposing potentially corrupted data to the consumer.
uncertain_points.cond: rx_valid_q high and (frame_err or rx_parity_err high)
uncertain_points.risk: Downstream logic may process erroneous data, violating an intended security policy of clearing or masking data on error.

uncertain_points.claim: In non-parity mode, rx_data selects sreg_q[9:2] instead of sreg_q[8:1]. This may include a stop bit or extra bit as data and drop a data LSB if the standard frame layout applies.
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect data extraction for no-parity frames, potentially causing functional errors or misinterpretation of received bytes.

uncertain_points.claim: rx_valid is directly driven from rx_valid_q without any qualification from frame_err or rx_parity_err, meaning the valid handshake is asserted even for corrupted frames.
uncertain_points.cond: frame_err or rx_parity_err true while rx_valid_q high
uncertain_points.risk: Consumers relying solely on the valid signal may accept and act on erroneous data, possibly bypassing error handling if they do not inspect error flags.
